summary.headline: Dodla Dairy Q4 FY26 revenue rose 18% to INR1,074 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 5% as milk procurement costs outran price hikes.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue hit a record INR1,074 crore (+18.1% YoY) on volume growth, but EBITDA margin compressed to 5% as procurement cost rose to INR41/litre from INR37.4 a year earlier while average milk sales price moved only to INR58.4/litre. Reported Q4 PAT of INR70 crore (6.5% margin) was flattered by about INR39 crore of one-offs; underlying Q4 PAT is about INR40 crore. FY26 adjusted PAT is about INR215 crore (5.2% margin) against reported INR267 crore. Management guides to a gradual 50-100 bps gross margin recovery in FY27 and low-to-mid-teens revenue growth, with procurement relief expected from June.

segments.name: India standalone
segments.commentary: Q4 milk procurement averaged 18.5 lakh litres/day (+13.4% YoY); procurement cost INR41/litre vs INR37.4 a year ago, and average milk sales price INR58.4/litre vs INR57.7 in Q3. Standalone India EBITDA margin for FY26 was about 6-7%, with Q4 described as a cyclical trough.

segments.name: Value-added products (VAP)
segments.commentary: Total VAP INR2,969 million vs INR2,841 million in Q4 FY25; excluding bulk sales, VAP grew 21% YoY. Curd rupee sales were INR230 crore in Q4 and INR845.7 crore in FY26; consolidated VAP realisation was INR60.54/litre.

segments.name: Africa (Uganda and Kenya)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR151 crore (+48% YoY) with liquid milk volume up more than 60%; record quarterly EBITDA of INR18 crore. FY26 EBITDA margin about 11.3% vs 11% in FY25, and FY26 volume about 2.27 lakh litres/day (Uganda about 1.5 lakh, Kenya about 0.9 lakh).

segments.name: OSAM / HR Food (OrgaFeed)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR81.9 crore (+23.2% YoY) with EBITDA INR2.7 crore; FY26 revenue INR214.7 crore and EBITDA INR4.8 crore. Management cites about 21% gross margin, targeting 25%, and a 6-12 month window to converge with company margins.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided to low-to-mid teens, supported by full-year OSAM consolidation, Africa on current trajectory, and 8-9% organic growth in India.
Gross margin to recover 50-100 bps over FY26 levels as procurement normalises and pricing actions take effect.
Effective tax rate to return to 25-27% after favourable ITAT orders in FY26; no further tax-credit impact from Q1 FY27.
Africa to reach 15-18% of consolidated revenue by FY28; Africa volume growth of about 20% targeted, implying about INR600 crore revenue vs about INR500 crore in FY26.
Management expects procurement to fall by roughly INR1-1.5/litre and a further rupee or so of price correction, with Q1 FY27 standalone margin recovery.
Capital allocation priority: growth capex (Maharashtra, Uganda, regular capex) from internal accruals, then regular dividends, then selective bolt-on acquisitions.
capex_capacity: Maharashtra project (total envelope INR280 crore): INR20 crore spent in FY25, INR86 crore in FY26, and about INR180 crore planned in FY27; commercial operations expected by end FY27.
FY27 standalone capex budget about INR130 crore, including INR65 crore regular capex and about INR7 crore hardware (excluding Maharashtra).
Uganda greenfield: 70 acres acquired, total capex about INR60 crore including land and plant, phased, completion by end FY29; Phase 2 adds pasteurised milk and milk products.
Bihar: 7-acre land allotted by BIADA for a dairy, with about INR4.4 crore land cost; subject to Board approval.
Maharashtra procurement averages about 3 lakh litres/day, with a target of at least 5 lakh litres/day by end of the season (around end of FY27).
demand_pricing: Company raised prices in mid-March 2026; cooperatives (Amul, Mother Dairy) followed with about INR2/litre hikes in May. Management says the next price action depends on fuel, packaging and freight stabilising, with only minor corrections planned in the near term.
Packaging material costs are up about 30% YoY (mainly plastics); expected to stay elevated as government excise support is temporary.
Freight: fuel up about INR3 recently; management said it will absorb for 15-30 days before passing on, with an estimated impact of about 0.25-0.5%.
Milk volume growth guided at 5-6% for liquid milk (about 9.4% including VAP in FY26); VAP growing 16-17% in the current season.
Procurement cost in mid-May was unchanged from March levels (INR41 consolidated, +9.7% YoY); the company says it has passed on about INR1/litre of the inflation so far.
Realisations: India milk INR58.25 vs INR56.15 YoY; HR Food milk INR55.7 and VAP INR98.8 vs Dodla India VAP INR64.2 (excluding fat products).
Management expects VAP mix to rise to 32-34% of revenue once expansions stabilise; seasonality in curd, buttermilk and lassi being addressed to extend demand from 2-3 months to about six months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the steady-state margin in this environment, and is the structural margin lower?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described FY27 as a cautious, transition year given fuel, plastic and agri-input uncertainty, and said margins can return to normal afterwards; another analyst confirmed the company expects margins to revert to mean by FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is procurement cost today versus the Q4 average, and how much inflation has been passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Procurement remains near March levels at about INR41/litre (+9.7% YoY consolidated, +9.3% standalone). About INR1/litre of inflation has been recovered so far, with another INR1-1.5 expected from procurement relief.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 capex breakup, and what were Q4 realisations?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 standalone capex about INR130 crore plus Maharashtra INR180 crore. Q4 consolidated realisation was INR61.19 per litre (INR56.16 for milk), and VAP realisation INR60.54 consolidated.

qa_highlights.question: How is OSAM margin expected to converge, and why did OrgaFeed margins drop?
qa_highlights.answer: OSAM margin improvement expected in 6-12 months via SAP, quality and logistics work, targeting about 25% gross margin. OrgaFeed margins fell from higher maize costs and freight for longer distances, but management says the margin is still about 11%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Africa split by country and EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: FY25 volume about 1.8 lakh litres/day (Uganda about 1.45 lakh, Kenya about 35,000); FY26 about 2.27 lakh (Uganda about 1.5 lakh, Kenya about 90,000). EBITDA margin about 11% in FY25 and 11.3% in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: How has the price-and-volume mix shifted in India?
qa_highlights.answer: Liquid milk volume grew about 5-6% YoY, VAP about 16%. Management says the company did not raise milk prices to protect market share and wants to keep the gap to cooperatives manageable.

risks_watch: Procurement normalisation is not yet visible: mid-May cost is unchanged, and the May-June recovery depends on Maharashtra and Karnataka productivity gains and on the southern states.
El Nino, drought and fuel price volatility (crude moves cited at USD60-120/barrel) could raise procurement, freight and packaging costs faster than prices can be passed on.
Q4 was flattered by about INR39 crore of one-offs (tax credit INR29 crore, interest income INR10 crore); FY27 PAT should be judged against about INR215 crore adjusted FY26.
OSAM and OrgaFeed margins are below the company average and depend on the pace of the SAP, logistics and procurement fixes.

Maharashtra greenfield (about INR180 crore to spend in FY27) and Uganda phase 2 raise execution risk and employee and other costs, which rose about 27% YoY in Q4 (employee) and about 15% (other expenses).
summary.management_tone: Confident on medium-term recovery and Africa growth, but cautious on near-term margins; management repeatedly stressed uncertainty over fuel, packaging and El Nino and chose to guide conservatively. Some answers were unclear or required clarification during the call.

financial_highlights.change: Includes INR29 crore tax credit and INR10 crore interest income; underlying about INR40 crore
Adjusted about INR215 crore, 5.2% margin after about INR70 crore one-offs
Includes INR271 crore HR Food expansion, INR86 crore Maharashtra, INR73 crore maintenance

key_quotes: Margins remained under pressure due to elevated milk procurement costs and a calibrated pricing strategy.
Going forward, the situation is turning positive. Milk supply is improving, which should result in a normalization of procurement costs for milk sales.
So this is more a '27 year kind of a year where, taking into consideration uncertainties versus what is going on, that we are trying to give this kind of a guidance.
Excluding these two one -off items, our Q4 underlying PAT is approximately INR40 crores.
This is the clean baseline against which FY '27 should be evaluated.

adds.what: Maharashtra dairy project (total envelope INR280 crore), commercial operations expected by end FY27
Uganda greenfield dairy (70 acres, phased; Phase 2 adds pasteurised milk and milk products), completion by end FY29

growth.why: FY27 revenue growth guided at low-to-mid teens (midpoint ~14%), backed by full-year OSAM consolidation, Africa volume growth of about 20% and 8-9% India organic growth; the Maharashtra plant (about INR180 crore FY27 spend, ops by end FY27) and procurement scale-up to 5 lakh litres/day give partial support, but no capacity or order figures tie directly to the revenue number.
